item.title: Edwin Shankar appointed ANZ Kiribati Country Head
item.description: Fijian banker, Edwin Shankar has been appointed the new Country Head of ANZ Kiribati, subject to regulatory approvals, and is expected to take up the role in early December. Shankar is currently Director Diversified Industries with ANZ Papua New Guinea and has more than 20 years of banking experience across Papua New Guinea, Fiji, Solomon Islands, Australia and the wider Pacific.
item.content:encoded:
Fijian banker, Edwin Shankar has been appointed the new Country Head of ANZ Kiribati, subject to regulatory approvals, and is expected to take up the role in early December.

Shankar is currently Director Diversified Industries with ANZ Papua New Guinea and has more than 20 years of banking experience across Papua New Guinea, Fiji, Solomon Islands, Australia and the wider Pacific.

He will report to ANZ Vanuatu Country Head Sucharu Tandon and succeed Greg Edwards, who has led ANZ Kiribati since 2019.

ANZ Regional Executive Pacific Sarah Stubbings says Shankar’s regional experience, customer relationships and leadership skills will be valuable in the role.

Stubbings says Kiribati remains an important market for ANZ, which is the country’s only commercial bank.

She says the bank remains committed to providing safe, reliable and accessible banking services while investing in its people, expanding digital access and supporting financial inclusion.

Shankar says he is privileged to be appointed to the role and looks forward to meeting customers, colleagues and stakeholders.

Earlier in his career, he served as Head of Treasury and Trade in Solomon Islands and held money market, balance sheet and foreign exchange roles in Fiji.

He holds an MBA Global with Distinction from James Cook University.

Stubbings has also thanked Edwards for his leadership, saying he helped maintain continuity of banking services through a period of significant change .

ANZ says Shankar will undertake a structured handover to ensure continuity for customers, colleagues and stakeholders.

item.title: Fijians get another cooling option as Gokals launches FUJITSU GENERAL air conditioners

item.content:encoded:
Fijians will have another option to beat the heat this hot season, with Gokals & Company Limited launching FUJITSU GENERAL air conditioners at its Pier Street office in Suva today.

Vinod Gokal, Director of Gokals, says the company is delighted to welcome the renowned Japanese brand back to its shelves after 30 years, describing its return as an exciting development given the product’s reputation for durability.

Gokals, a leading consumer electronics retailer and distributor in Fiji and the South Pacific, proudly represents internationally recognised brands such as Philips, Whirlpool and Mitsubishi.

Gokal says the addition of FUJITSU GENERAL further strengthens the company’s product range, providing customers with more choices to meet their cooling needs.

He says the presence of the company’s partners from New Zealand at the launch reflects their confidence in the product and its potential to expand into Fiji’s corporate market.

The Japanese Ambassador was also present at the launch.

Gokal adds the company remains committed to bringing together a comprehensive range of electronic appliances and technology solutions to meet the needs and expectations of Fijians in both the residential and corporate sectors.

item.title: FMF Foods launches Amul Condensed Milk
item.description: Fijians will have another option for preparing desserts and sweet treats this Diwali, following the launch of Amul Condensed Milk by FMF Foods Limited at the FMF IDC Finals. The new product adds to the company's Amul range in Fiji, following the success of Amul Ghee, which has become a favourite among local consumers.
item.content:encoded:
Fijians will have another option for preparing desserts and sweet treats this Diwali, following the launch of Amul Condensed Milk by FMF Foods Limited at the FMF IDC Finals.

The new product adds to the company's Amul range in Fiji, following the success of Amul Ghee, which has become a favourite among local consumers.

FMF Foods says the condensed milk is suitable for preparing desserts, beverages and traditional family recipes.

The launch was marked by a performance from the Mata Dance Group, while guests were also given the opportunity to sample dishes prepared using the product.

These included kheer-puri, custard pie, gulab jamun and roti, showcasing its use in a range of traditional dishes and sweet treats.

FMF Foods, the naming rights sponsor of the FMF IDC, chose the championship finals as the occasion to introduce the new product, bringing together the country's passion for football and its love for food.

The company says the launch marks another step in expanding its product range and bringing more choices to households across Fiji.
